To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MILCA have the capacity to function as a bioartificial liver support device.

1) MILCA have a structure and function that is similar to that of a normal human liver, 2) they can be inoculated into hollow fibers and function as a bioartificial liver, 3) they can be used in the treatment of fulminant hepetic failure.

1) MILCA are formed by seeding collagen-coated beads with hepatocytes; 2) MILCA are viable and metabolically functional for up to 24 hours in static culture and 6 hours in a hollow-fiber bioprocess; 3) MILCA are structurally similar to liver parenchyma on transmission electron microscopy; 4) MILCA can be inoculated into a bioreactor and perfused with patient plasma for up to 6 hours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a bioartificial liver using hepatocyte aggregates as the source of functional liver tissue.
the development of bioartificial liver systems that can be used for the treatment of patients with acute liver failure.
development of a bioartificial liver device for treatment of acute liver failure in humans.
